title: Schools and confessions: principles are Scripture itself
source_text: XIV. Verum ad pleniorem quaestionis hujus intelligentiam, hic quoque est animadvertendum, ea quae in scholis nostris tractari solent, & in publicis nostrorum confessionibus proponi, & exponi, vel consistere in admissione verorum principiorum fidei & religionis, & rejectione eorum quae pro talibus principiis immerito & falso obtruduntur: vel esse doctrinam ipsam ex veris principiis haustam atque deductam. Et fidei quidem principia Scriptura sacra contineri dicimus, quoniam sunt ipsa Scriptura. Nec enim Ecclesiae nostrae ulla fidei principia admittunt, praeter libros divinitus inspiratos quibus constat Scripturae corpus.
pass_a_gloss: But for a fuller understanding of this question, here also it is to be observed that those things which are wont to be treated in our schools, and to be proposed and set forth in the public confessions of our people, either consist in the admission of the true principles of faith and religion, and the rejection of those which are undeservedly and falsely thrust forward as such principles: or are the doctrine itself drawn and deduced from the true principles. And we say that the principles of faith are contained by sacred Scripture, because they are Scripture itself. For neither do our Churches admit any principles of faith besides the books divinely inspired of which the body of Scripture consists.
pass_b_english: For a fuller grasp of the question, note what our schools treat and our public confessions set out. Some of it is admitting the true principles of faith and religion, and rejecting what is falsely pushed forward as such. The rest is the doctrine drawn from those true principles.

We say Scripture contains the principles of faith because those principles are Scripture itself. Our Churches admit no principles of faith beyond the inspired books that make up the body of Scripture.

choices.why: Identity claim, not a higher canon beside the books.
